page_title: Function Multiversioning (Using the GNU Compiler Collection (GCC))

sources.entry: Function Multiversioning (GCC) - Defines target_clones, one function per ISA behind a resolver the dynamic linker runs, so a generic build ships AVX-512.

summary.title: Function Multiversioning (Using the GNU Compiler Collection (GCC))
summary.one_liner: GCC's function multiversioning compiles several versions of one function specialized for different architecture extensions and uses a runtime resolver to pick the right one.
keywords: how to compile multiple versions of a function gcc
takeaways: Function multiversioning builds several versions of a function, each targeting different architecture extensions, plus a resolver that selects one at runtime.
It depends on the ELF indirect function (ifunc) extension, requiring Binutils 2.20.1 or higher and GNU C Library 2.11.1 or higher.
On AArch64, LoongArch and RISC-V, versions are declared with target_version and target_clones attributes, which can span translation units in C or C++.
On x86, versions are declared with the target attribute (multiple definitions in C++) or a single definition using target_clones.
A version with target "default" is used when no other version qualifies on the running platform; callers just call the function or take its address.
summary.summary: The GCC manual page explains function multiversioning, where the compiler generates multiple specialized versions of a function plus a resolver that the dynamic linker uses to choose one at runtime. It states the requirements (Binutils 2.20.1+, glibc 2.11.1+) and describes two versions of the feature: the target_version/target_clones attributes for AArch64, LoongArch and RISC-V (with a C/C++ multi-file example), and the target attribute for x86. The x86 example shows a default version plus variants for sse4.2, arch=atom and arch=amdfam10, with callers invoking foo normally. The page points to the GCC wiki for further details.
